name: EMBER DECK
thesis: The current app fails because it made *restraint* the whole idea: hairlines, prose, no icons, no faces, no surfaces. It reads as a document because it is one. EMBER DECK keeps the two things worth keeping — the warm espresso ground (the seeded photography was generated on #13–18 warm grounds, so places dissolve into the page instead of floating on a blue-grey slab) and the ember/gold accent grammar (order vs. label) — and replaces everything structural. Content moves onto raised cards with real radius and dark-UI elevation; every row is led by a photograph and a stack of the actual faces who cosigned it; every card carries a dense icon+value metadata strip; navigation becomes a five-slot icon tab bar with a raised ember compose FAB in the centre. Prose paragraphs are cut to at most one line per surface and their content is re-expressed as chips, tiles, and meta strips — which is also how "not enough features" gets fixed, because the six built-but-buried features (head-to-head, collaborative lists, group sessions, friends, activity, Maps import) all get a permanent door. The founder's "AI slop" is the editorial-serif-on-hairlines look; the fix is not more restraint, it is a saturated, photographic, people-first product that still refuses to have a single like button anywhere in it.

palette.strategy: Stay warm, go hotter and deeper. A saturated accent on a near-black warm ground is more distinctive than the dribbble-default saturated blue/purple, and it is the one part of the current system the seeded imagery is already tuned to. The ground goes DARKER (so raised cards have somewhere to rise from) and the accent goes HOTTER. All contrast is re-derived against --surface (the card ground), not --bg, because after this change almost no text sits on --bg any more — that is the single most common way a card retrofit silently breaks WCAG.

ground.--sunk: 22 20% 4%  /* #0D0A08 — the tab bar, the space behind cards, sheet scrim base */
ground.--bg: 22 16% 6%  /* #120E0C — page ground, one step darker than today's #14100E */
ground.--surface: 22 15% 10% /* #1D1815 — the card. The default reading ground now. */
ground.--raise: 22 16% 14% /* #292322 — pressed card, wells, inactive segmented control */
ground.--tint: hsl(var(--pal) / 0.07) /* a place's own hue washed into its card header */

ink.--line: 32 26% 78% /* #D5C8B8 — the honest line, body copy.  10.66:1 on --surface */
ink.--muted: 31 14% 60% /* #A79A8B — metadata, meta strip values.  6.34:1 on --surface (today's 54% would fall to ~4.2:1 once it sits on a card — this is the required re-derivation) */

accents.--ember: 13 88% 57% /* #F25A31 — THE accent. Rank numerals, the FAB, the active tab, selected chips, the save action.  5.25:1 on --surface, 5.78:1 on --bg */
accents.--ember-wash: hsl(var(--ember) / 0.14) /* tinted circles behind empty-state icons, the hero card ground */
accents.--gold: 41 62% 62% /* #DAB462 — the label voice only: small-caps section labels, the ask count.  8.92:1 on --surface */
accents.rule: Ember has two jobs (the ORDER, and the ACT of writing) and gold has one (the LABEL voice). Preserved verbatim from the current system. Neither is ever a large-area background — the hero card is a 14% ember wash, not solid ember.

rules.--rule: 22 14% 18% /* card borders, dividers inside a card */
rules.note: Hairlines survive but demoted: they now divide WITHIN a card. Between cards, the gap and the elevation do the work.

placeHues.note: The six --pal-* / --plate-* palettes carry over UNCHANGED. They are what stops this from being a monochrome app — each card's rank chip, plate, and 7% header wash take the hue its photograph was painted from, so a scrolling feed has colour rhythm drawn from the places rather than applied on top of them.

elevation.--elev-1: inset 0 1px 0 hsl(0 0% 100% / 0.045), 0 2px 8px hsl(20 40% 2% / 0.55)  /* the standard card */
elevation.--elev-2: inset 0 1px 0 hsl(0 0% 100% / 0.06), 0 10px 28px hsl(20 40% 2% / 0.6)   /* sheets, the hero card */
elevation.note: Dark-UI elevation is a 1px inset top highlight FIRST and a shadow second. Shadow alone on a near-black ground is invisible; the highlight is what makes the card read as lifted.

antiSlop: No purple, no blue-violet, no gradient from two brand colours.
No glassmorphism on cards — backdrop-blur is used in exactly one place, the tab bar.
No white or light-grey cards. Ever.
Colour saturation lives in photography and the six place hues; the chrome stays near-black.

typography:
Drop Young Serif and Karla entirely — the editorial serif IS the look the founder rejected, and Karla is its companion. Two self-hosted OFL families, four woff2 files, no CDN.

DISPLAY — **Bricolage Grotesque 800** (`--font-display`). A wide, slightly irregular grotesque with real personality: it reads as a product with an opinion, not as a magazine and not as Inter. Used for: screen titles, place names on cards ≥19px, rank numerals (tabular figures), the hero answer, stat figures.
UI/BODY — **Schibsted Grotesk 400 / 500 / 700** (`--font-body`). Warm-toned, excellent at 13–15px, unmistakably not Inter. Used for: everything you read, meta strips, chips, tab labels, buttons.

Scale (rebuilt around cards; the old 1.22 ratio kept, sizes pushed up because a card gives things room):
  --text-2xs 0.6875rem/11px  small-caps labels, tab labels (700, 0.10em tracking)
  --text-xs  0.8125rem/13px  meta-strip values, timestamps, captions
  --text-sm  0.9375rem/15px  the one honest line, body inside a card
  --text-base 1rem/16px      minimum body
  --text-lg  1.1875rem/19px  place name on a card (Bricolage 800, -0.02em)
  --text-xl  1.4375rem/23px  section titles / sheet titles
  --text-2xl 1.75rem/28px    rank numerals, stat figures
  --text-3xl 2.25rem/36px    screen title
  --text-4xl 3rem/48px       the hero answer, head-to-head place names

  --tracking-display -0.022em (tighter than today's -0.012em; Bricolage 800 needs it)
  --tracking-caps 0.10em (down from 0.14em — small-caps at 0.14em on a dense card reads as shouting)
  --leading-tight 1.02 · --leading-snug 1.18 · --leading-body 1.5

PROSE BUDGET, enforced by review: at most ONE explanatory sentence per screen, at most two lines. Every other paragraph currently on Home, Search, Profile and the group pages must become a chip, a meta value, or a tooltip-free label. This is 60% of the "too many words" complaint and it is a copy pass, not a design one — schedule it as its own commit.

FONT WEIGHT ON THE SSR PAGES: the public share page and public profile load exactly TWO faces (Bricolage 800 + Schibsted 400), latin-basic subset, `<link rel=preload>` in the SSR head, `font-display: swap`. The SPA loads all four. This is not fussiness — the Phase 5A/6 measurements price the fonts at ~335 ms of a 1000 ms LCP budget with ~53 ms of slack, so a third face on the share page is the difference between passing and not.
shape:
RADIUS — the documented "no radius above 3px except the two pills" rule is explicitly repealed. It is the single strongest signal of the rejected look.
  --radius-card 18px   the card, the hero, tiles
  --radius-media 14px  photos inside a card (card radius minus the 4px inset)
  --radius-sheet 22px  bottom sheets, top corners only
  --radius-chip 999px  chips, pills, the FAB, avatars
  --radius-sm 6px      inputs, small tiles, the rank chip
  Nothing in the product uses a radius that is not one of these five.

SURFACE — a card is: `--surface` ground, 1px `--rule` border, `--radius-card`, `--elev-1`, 14px internal padding (16px on the content block, 4px inset around a photo). Cards sit on `--bg` with a 10px gap in a vertical feed and a 12px gap in a horizontal snap rail.

DENSITY — a feed card is roughly 168px tall (compact, no photo: 96px). A 390×844 screen shows the hero card plus two and a half feed cards, which is the density target: something is always cut off at the bottom, so the feed reads as deep.

PRESS — a card answers a finger in `--duration-fast`: ground to `--raise`, `transform: scale(0.995)`, shadow to none. That is the existing PRESS verb applied to a new shape, not a new verb.

STRUCTURE INSIDE A CARD — the hairline survives here and only here: a 1px `--rule` divider between a card's content block and its cosign row. This is how the old vocabulary earns its place instead of being deleted out of spite.

MEDIA — every place card leads with its 16:10 photograph or its designed no-photo plate in the place's own hue. No card in the product is text-only except the two ledger/stat shapes.
icons:
A VENDORED set. `src/components/icons/` — one `paths.ts` (a `Record<IconName, string>` of `d` attributes) plus `Icon.tsx` (a typed `name` union → `<svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round">`), and the ISC `LICENSE` file traced-from Lucide's geometry. Roughly 4 kB for the whole set. **Do not reinstall `lucide-react`** — that reintroduces a dependency the Phase 6 purge removed and ships 1,400 icons to get 26; hard rule 7 wants it vendored, not fetched.

The 26 icons, and each one's single job:
  compass (Home) · search · plus (the FAB / Log) · users (Crew) · user (You, fallback when no avatar)
  bell (activity) · map-pin (distance) · clock (hours) · plug (outlets) · wifi · sound (noise) · seat (seating) · sun (natural light) · door (bathroom code) · cup (drip/latte price) · moon (late hours)
  shuffle (head-to-head) · list-ordered (your ranked list) · layers (collaborative lists) · circle-dot (a live group session)
  check · x · chevron-right · chevron-left · share · refresh (still accurate?)

BANNED FROM THE SET, permanently: star, heart, thumb, flame, trophy, medal, fire, bar-chart, gauge, any partially-filled glyph. Two of those are literally caught by `no-scales.test.ts`'s glyph rule; the rest are banned because they are the visual grammar of rating and of engagement bait, and an icon set is exactly where they sneak back in.

THE PARTIAL-FILL RULE (the one that will actually be violated): `wifi` and `sound` look like level meters. They are drawn at FULL state always, and never rendered with n-of-3 arcs lit to indicate a level — that is a graphical rating scale that `no-scales.test.ts` cannot see. The level is always the labelled enum word beside the icon (`quiet` / `conversational` / `loud`), and the icon is `aria-hidden`.

ICONS NEVER CARRY MEANING ALONE (hard rule 8): every icon in a meta strip has its value in text immediately to its right; every icon-only control has an `aria-label`; every tab has a visible 11px text label under its glyph. Icon size: 14px in a meta strip, 18px in a chip, 22px in the tab bar, 26px in the FAB, 20px inside the tinted circle of an empty state.
navigation:
A FIVE-SLOT BOTTOM BAR: four destinations plus one action in the centre. The brief's "at most four primary destinations" is honoured exactly — the FAB is not a destination, it is the compose action, and it is the only reason the bar has five slots.

  1. HOME    (compass)  →  /            discovery, the hero query, the crew feed
  2. SEARCH  (search)   →  /search      places / people / lists, filter rail
  3. LOG     (plus, FAB, ember)  →  /log      raised 14px above the bar, 60px circle, --elev-fab
  4. CREW    (users)    →  /crew        NEW HUB — friends, requests, lists, group sessions, activity
  5. YOU     (the user's own avatar, 26px, ember 2px ring when active) → /:username

`.cs-tabbar`: 62px tall + `env(safe-area-inset-bottom)`, `--sunk` ground at 0.86 alpha with `backdrop-filter: blur(14px)`, 1px `--rule` top border. Inactive glyph `--muted`; active glyph `--ember` with an 18px 2px ember rule drawn under the label (the DRAW verb, unchanged). Each slot is a 56×62 target.

TOP APP BAR per screen: 52px, transparent over the scroll, title left in Bricolage 800 at 19px, one or two 44px icon actions right. Home's right action is `bell` carrying the ask count (a 16px gold dot with a tabular numeral) — the exact same count `AppShell.tsx` already computes, which can only be raised by a friend request or a friend asking, is never raised by elapsed time, and is cleared by answering.

THE CREW HUB is the answer to "not enough features". One screen, a segmented control across the top, and six built features finally have a door:
  Friends   — roster, pending requests as actionable rows, add-by-username
  Lists     — collaborative lists you're in, "New list" primary
  Groups    — live sessions (circle-dot, pulsing? no — static), "Start a group decision" primary
  Activity  — the notification feed, moved out of the bottom of Profile

SECONDARY REACH — nothing lives in one place only:
  · Head-to-head (/rank) reaches from You → "Rank your places", from a place card's overflow → "Rank it", and from the post-save log screen.
  · Maps Takeout import moves OUT of /rank's empty state (where it vanishes forever once you rank one place — a real bug) into Onboarding step 3 AND You → Import, permanently.
  · Share-token management gets a `share` action in the Profile app bar opening a sheet: copy link, see who has it, revoke.
  · "Add to a list" is an overflow action on every place card.

NO hamburger, no drawer, no nested tab-within-tab beyond the one segmented control on Crew and the one on Profile. Every screen is at most two taps from any tab.
components: `.cs-card` — the base. --surface ground, 1px --rule, --radius-card, --elev-1, 14px pad. Press: --raise + scale(.995) in --duration-fast. Everything below is a specialisation of this.

`.cs-place-card` — THE feed unit and the thing the founder will judge. 16:10 photo (or the hue plate) at --radius-media inset 4px; an ember rank chip absolute top-left when the place is in somebody's ranked list; content block: name (Bricolage 800 / 19px / --ink), one honest line (15px / --line / 2-line clamp), meta strip; a 1px --rule divider; then the cosign row. Whole card is one link, keeps `data-place` / `data-shop-id` / `data-shop-slug`.

`.cs-meta` — the density workhorse. A wrapping flex row of 14px icon + 13px --muted value pairs with 3px dot separators: `map-pin 6 min · clock till 11pm · plug 12 outlets · sound quiet`. Four to six per card. This single component converts most of the app's rejected prose into visible capability.

`.cs-cosign-row` — the social proof, and the thing that is NOT an engagement row. An overlapping avatar stack (up to 4, then `+N`) plus one sentence: 'Maya, Lena and 3 others cosign this'. NO like, NO reply, NO repost, NO counts of anything you can do to a post. Tapping it opens the cosigners sheet.

`.cs-avatar` — 24 / 32 / 44 / 72 / 96px, --radius-chip, 1.5px --bg ring, --surface fallback ground with the user's initials in their hue. `.cs-avatar-stack` overlaps at -9px with a 2px --bg ring per avatar, `direction: rtl` trick so the first avatar sits on top. A standalone avatar target gets an invisible 44px hit box.

`.cs-rank-chip` — a 26px --radius-sm ember square holding a tabular numeral in --bg. This is the ONE place a number appears next to a place, and it is a position in an ordered list, never a score. `data-rank`.

`.cs-chip` — KEPT (disabled.test.ts names it). Restyled: 36px visual height with an 8px vertical ::before hit extension to clear 44px, --radius-chip, 1px --rule-strong border, optional 18px leading icon, 13px/500 label. Selected = solid --ember with --bg text. One solid ember chip per single-select group, unchanged.
`.cs-chip-rail` — horizontally scrolling chip row with 18px edge fade, `scroll-snap-type: x proximity`, `-webkit-overflow-scrolling`. Search filters, place facts, group needs.

`.cs-fab` — 60px ember circle, --elev-fab, `plus` at 26px in --bg, centred in the tab bar and raised 14px above it. Press: scale(.94) + shadow collapse in --duration-fast. Keeps `data-log-entry` so the existing prefetch-on-pointerdown warming survives.
`.cs-pill` / `.cs-pill-ghost` — KEPT (disabled.test.ts). Radius goes to --radius-chip, height stays 44px, solid ember commits / outline is everything after the commit. Unchanged semantics.
`.cs-word` — KEPT. Now always gets `min-width: var(--tap)` baked into the class rather than at each call site, which is the bug Phase 4 and Phase 5B both hit.

`.cs-sheet` — bottom sheet: --surface, --radius-sheet on the top corners only, --elev-2, a 36×4px --rule-strong grab handle, scrim `hsl(var(--sunk)/0.7)`. Arrives with SETTLE (translateY 12px + fade over --duration-base). Used for: filters, cosigners, add-to-list, share & revoke, install-to-home-screen. This is how features get reachable without new routes.

`.cs-segment` — segmented control, --raise track at --radius-chip, --surface thumb, 44px tall, 2–4 items. Crew's four sections, Profile's three, Search's three. Not a tab bar, not a radiogroup — plain buttons with `aria-pressed`, because `role=radiogroup` is banned by no-scales.test.ts.
`.cs-stat` — a profile-header figure: 28px Bricolage tabular numeral over an 11px gold small-caps label. Three per row on a --raise strip inside the header card.

`.cs-tile` — the functional-facts grid on a place page: 2-up (3-up on desktop) --raise squares at --radius-sm, 20px icon, 11px gold label, 15px --ink value. Outlets / wifi / noise now / seating / natural light / camp-able / bathroom / price / late hours. Nine tiles is what 'feature-rich' actually looks like, and it is data the seed already carries.

`.cs-versus` — the head-to-head shape. Two full-bleed place cards stacked with a 44px ember-outlined 'or' disc between them; each card is one enormous tap target; a 13px --muted line under: 'Which would you send a friend to?'. No slider, no scale, no drag. Keeps `data-side`.

`.cs-hero` — Home's answer card: --ember-wash ground, 1px `hsl(var(--ember)/0.3)` border, --radius-card, --elev-2. The query as an 11px gold small-caps label, the place name at 36–48px Bricolage, its photo as a 96px --radius-media thumb on the right, the meta strip beneath, and a 44px 'Ask again' ghost pill. Keeps `data-hero-query` / `data-hero-summary` / `data-ask-again`.

`.cs-activity-row` — 44px avatar + one sentence in --line with the actor's name in --ink + a 13px --muted relative timestamp + an optional inline action pill (Accept / Not now). Human actions only. Keeps `data-feed` / `data-ask`.
`.cs-section` — a section header: 11px gold small-caps title on the left, a 13px --ember-ink 'See all' text button with a `chevron-right` on the right. 44px tall.
`.cs-rail` — horizontal snap carousel of place cards at 78vw width, 12px gap, `scroll-snap-type: x mandatory`, 18px edge padding so the first card's shadow is not clipped. Home's 'Open now near you'.

`.cs-empty` — Nothing.tsx restyled: a 64px --ember-wash circle with a 26px ember icon, an 19px Bricolage title, one 15px --line sentence, one 44px primary pill. Keeps `data-nothing`. Every empty state is designed (brief #9) and this is the one shape they all use.

`.cs-skel` — STATIC skeleton blocks: --raise at --radius-sm, no shimmer, no pulse. A shimmer is `infinite` and `motion.test.ts` fails the suite on it, correctly — an animation no reduced-motion rule can stop is exactly what the ban is for.
`.cs-ledger` — KEPT for counts only (the group page's 'how 22 became 6', the shared list's 'who keeps it'), now inside a card. Its value column is still `white-space: nowrap`, so still never prose.
screens: HOME — app bar (COSIGN / bell+count). `.cs-hero` answer card. `.cs-rail` 'Open now near you' (horizontal place cards). `.cs-section` 'From your crew' → 3–4 `.cs-activity-row`s with 'See all' → /crew. `.cs-section` 'Everywhere else on campus' → vertical `.cs-place-card` feed, with the existing friends/crowd order toggle kept as a `.cs-chip` pair rather than an underlined sentence. Finals week inserts a 'Still open in four hours' rail. The three long paragraphs currently on this screen collapse to one 13px line.

SEARCH — sticky search field in a --raise well, `.cs-segment` Places / People / Lists, `.cs-chip-rail` (Open now · Outlets · Quiet · Can camp · Late · Cheap · Near me), results as compact `.cs-place-card`s (96px, thumb-left). Empty query state shows recent + 'Cosigned near you' rather than a blank screen.

PLACE — 240px cover photo bleeding under the app bar, name at 36px overlapping the photo's bottom edge on a gradient scrim, `.cs-meta` strip, primary action row (ember `Rank it` pill + ghost `Log a visit` pill + `share`/overflow icons), `.cs-cosign-row` expanded into a full avatar list, the 9-tile `.cs-tile` facts grid, noise-by-time as three labelled enum chips, a freshness stamp + `refresh` 'Still accurate?' action, then 'Also cosigned by people who cosign this'.

LOG FLOW — unchanged mechanics, six steps, ≤10s budget intact. Each step is one `.cs-card` of large tap targets: photo (optional, camera tile), intent tags as a `.cs-chip` grid (the differentiator — make these the biggest chips in the product), enum taps for noise/seating, one optional short line. Progress stays a SENTENCE ('Two more, then you're done') — never a dot row, never a bar. Keeps every `data-step` / `data-option` / `data-value` / `data-save` attribute.

HEAD-TO-HEAD (/rank) — full-screen `.cs-versus`. A 13px --muted line above: 'This is comparison 3 of at most 5.' Exit is a `.cs-word` BACK. Reachable from You, from a place card overflow, and from the log-save screen.
YOUR LIST — the ranked list as `.cs-place-card`s with `.cs-rank-chip`, an app-bar `share` action, and a top strip: 'Your 22 places · last changed 3 days ago'. No drag handles.

CREW — `.cs-segment` Friends / Lists / Groups / Activity. Friends: pending requests as `.cs-activity-row`s with inline Accept/Not now, then the roster as avatar rows. Lists: `.cs-card` per collaborative list with a contributor avatar stack and a 'New list' FAB-adjacent pill. Groups: live sessions + 'Start a group decision'. Activity: the notification feed, human actions only.

LIST DETAIL — header card with the list name, contributor avatar stack, and the `.cs-ledger` 'how it merges'; then the merged order as ranked place cards; 'Add a place' pill. The server's derived-order privacy fix stays exactly as built.

GROUP SESSION — seats as 44px avatars in a row with empty seats as dashed circles, each person's needs as `.cs-chip`s, a live count card ('22 places → 6 that work for everyone'), then the intersection as place cards. Seat ids stay opaque.
GROUP NEW — one card: pick your needs as chips, get a link, a `.cs-sheet` to share it.

PROFILE (You / :username) — a cover band generated from the person's #1 place's palette hue (a 160px --tint gradient over their top photo at 18% alpha), a 96px avatar overlapping it, name in Bricolage 36px, school + one-line taste summary, a three-up `.cs-stat` row (Ranked · Logged this term · Friends), a `share` app-bar action opening the token sheet, then `.cs-segment` List / Logs / Lists.
ONBOARDING — three cards: who you are, your school, and IMPORT YOUR SAVED PLACES (Maps Takeout) — which now has a permanent second home in You → Import so it cannot disappear.
PUBLIC SHARE PAGE /s/:token — SSR, see sharePageStrategy.
PUBLIC PROFILE /p/:token — SSR, same treatment, keeps the existing data-URI SVG map plate (inlining it cost 737ms of style+layout; do not undo that).
INSTALL SHEET — a `.cs-sheet` reached from You → 'Add Cosign to your phone', with the iOS Share→Add-to-Home-Screen instructions illustrated and the Android `beforeinstallprompt` button.
mobileApp:
An INSTALLABLE PWA, and specifically a PWA with NO service worker. That is not a compromise, it is the only shape the rules allow: `no-bait.test.ts` bans the identifiers `serviceWorker`, `PushManager`, `showNotification` and `Notification.requestPermission` outright, so there is no offline cache and no push — which is exactly the intent of hard rule 3, since a push channel is the delivery mechanism for every form of engagement bait. Say that out loud in the install sheet: "It goes on your home screen. It will never send you a notification you didn't ask a person for."

What to build:
· `manifest.json` — `display: "standalone"`, `orientation: "portrait"`, `theme_color` and `background_color` both the new `--bg` hex (`#120E0C`), `start_url: "/"`, `scope: "/"`. NOTE: `tokens.test.ts` guards the six hand-written copies of the ground (index.html, manifest twice, and three `<meta name="theme-color">` tags) — all six change together in the token commit or the suite goes red.
· Icons: 192, 512, and a 512 `purpose: "maskable"` with a 20% safe-area inset — an ember monogram on `--bg`, generated locally into `public/icons/`, no external service.
· iOS: `<link rel="apple-touch-icon">`, `<meta name="apple-mobile-web-app-capable" content="yes">`, `<meta name="apple-mobile-web-app-status-bar-style" content="black-translucent">`.
· Safe areas: the tab bar pads with `env(safe-area-inset-bottom)`, the app bar with `env(safe-area-inset-top)`, and `html { scroll-padding-bottom: 6.5rem }` (up from 5rem — the bar got taller).
· Native feel: `overscroll-behavior-y: none` on body, `-webkit-tap-highlight-color: transparent` (already there), `touch-action: manipulation` on every pressable, `user-select: none` on chrome, momentum scrolling on the rails.
· `beforeinstallprompt` captured on Android and surfaced in the install sheet; iOS gets the illustrated three-step instead.
· Add a `display-mode: standalone` media query that hides the browser-chrome-compensating top padding.

EXPLICITLY NOT: Capacitor, Expo, a wrapper, an app-store build. All of them are external services or native toolchains, and hard rule 7 forecloses them. The honest sentence for the founder is: "It installs to the home screen, opens full-screen with no browser bar, and looks like an app — it is not in the App Store, and nothing in the brief lets it be."
sharePageStrategy:
The share page gets the NEW LOOK, in a deliberately cheaper dialect. It has to — it is the hero surface and the thing that gets sent, so it cannot be the one screen still in the rejected style. But it is judged against ~1.0s LCP on simulated Slow-4G with about 53ms of measured slack, so every element is priced.

WHAT IT GETS: the new palette, the new radius, cards, the rank chip, the author header with a real 72px photo, the meta strip, the filter chips (already there), and the new type — all of it pure CSS inlined by `server/pages/tokens.ts` exactly as today. No stylesheet request, no `/assets/*.js`; `e2e/share.spec.ts` already asserts zero of both and that assertion stays.

WHAT IT DOES NOT GET, and why each one is priced:
· TWO font faces only (Bricolage 800 + Schibsted 400), latin-basic subset, preloaded. The fonts already cost ~335ms of the budget; a third face is the whole slack.
· ONE shadow value, not two. `--elev-1` only, and it is applied to the entry cards via a single shared class — 20 cards with an identical box-shadow composite on one layer, not per-card variation.
· NO avatar stack on entries. Each avatar is a network request, and 20 entries × 3 faces is 60 requests on Slow-4G. The author's single photo is the only face on the page, and cosigners are named in text.
· AT MOST 4 inline icon glyphs total (map-pin, clock, plug, sound), written as raw `<svg>` in the template, `aria-hidden`, no sprite, no `<use>`.
· NO backdrop-filter anywhere. It is a compositing cost with no payoff on a page that does not scroll under chrome.
· NO carousel, no snap rail, no JS beyond the existing inline chip filter — and remember the trap: a `//` comment inside `PAGE_JS` is shredded by the `.replace(/\n/g,"")` and silently kills every brace after it, and a backtick in a `PAGE_CSS` comment ends the template literal. Keep commentary outside both.
· The `.cs-column` arrival cascade is SPA-only. Animating the LCP element is how you lose 300ms and how a `fullPage` screenshot catches rows mid-fade.

MEASUREMENT PROTOCOL, non-negotiable before sign-off: kill every stray Chrome process, then run `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 node scripts/lighthouse.mjs /s/<token> <phase> share` with `LH_RUNS=5` and take the median, then run it again with `LH_BLOCK="*/fonts/*"` to price the fonts, and run the OLD build in the same minute as a control. The font/LCP race on localhost is a coin flip worth ±450ms — a single run proves nothing.

The OG image (`server/pages/og.ts`) restyles too: new ground, new ember, the author's photo, the top three place names. Remember resvg cannot read the committed `.woff` files, so anything still live as text inside a nested SVG is dropped — compose in satori, which converts its own text to paths.
conflictsResolved: CARDS vs. HAIRLINES — cards win everywhere; hairlines survive only INSIDE a card, as the one divider between its content block and its cosign row. A hairline-only system is what made the app read as a document, but deleting hairlines entirely would throw away the one piece of the old vocabulary that still does a job.

SATURATED ACCENT vs. WARM ESPRESSO GROUND — keep the warm ground and hot up the accent (#E0633C → #F25A31), rather than adopting the dribbble-default saturated blue. The seeded photography was generated on warm #13–18 grounds, so a cool ground would make every photo float on a slab, and warm-on-warm is the more distinctive product.

ICONS EVERYWHERE vs. 'NO ICONS AT ALL' — icons win, but vendored as ~4kB of inline SVG paths with a hand-picked 26-icon set, not by reinstalling lucide-react. The old no-icon rule was a taste position; hard rule 7 is a real constraint and it only forbids fetching, not drawing.
FIVE-SLOT TAB BAR vs. THE BRIEF'S 'AT MOST FOUR DESTINATIONS' — both hold, because the fifth slot is the compose FAB and a FAB is an action, not a destination. Home / Search / Crew / You is four.

AVATAR-LED ROWS vs. PHASE 5B'S 'NO AVATAR ON ANY 5B SURFACE' — avatars win and that rule is repealed. It existed because a column of monograms on a page with six people reads as an avatar row by another name; that was precisely the complaint. Real photographs, not monograms, and a monogram only as the fallback.

A PROFILE STATS ROW vs. 'NO VANITY METRICS' — three stats and no more: Ranked, Logged this term, Friends. All three are set sizes the person controls, none is comparative, none is ranked against other users, and there is no profile-view count, no reach, no follower number. A count of your own things is inventory; a count of other people's attention is vanity.

TWITTER'S ENGAGEMENT ROW vs. COSIGN-ONLY — the visual density of an engagement row is kept and its semantics are deleted. `.cs-cosign-row` is an avatar stack plus a sentence naming who ranked the place. There is no like, no reply, no repost, no heart, no counter of anything you can do to a post. This is the single most important line in the direction: the dribbble baseline's densest component is also its most forbidden one, and the graft is form without function.

SHIMMER SKELETONS vs. `motion.test.ts` — skeletons are static tinted blocks. A shimmer is `animation: … infinite`, which the test correctly fails, because reduced motion here is implemented by zeroing four duration tokens and an infinite loop is an animation nobody can stop.

DRAG-TO-REORDER YOUR LIST vs. HEAD-TO-HEAD-ONLY — no drag handles. Dragging is not a rating scale and would technically pass `no-scales.test.ts`, but it is a direct-ordering input that routes around the comparison mechanic that IS the product's cosign. Re-ordering is always a head-to-head.

EDITORIAL SERIF vs. INTER-EVERYWHERE — neither. Bricolage Grotesque 800 for display and Schibsted Grotesk for UI. The serif is the rejected look; Inter is the slop tell the evidence rules already name.
RADIUS ABOVE 3px vs. THE DOCUMENTED BAN — repealed, and replaced with a five-value radius scale. 'This is print, not a card deck' was the position that produced the app the founder hates.

BOTTOM SHEETS vs. 'THREE MOTION VERBS AND DELIBERATELY NO FOURTH' — no fourth verb. A sheet arriving is SETTLE (translateY + fade over --duration-base); a tab activating is DRAW; a card answering a finger is PRESS. The vocabulary was built to absorb this.

A NATIVE APP vs. ZERO EXTERNAL SERVICES — an installable PWA with no service worker. Capacitor/Expo/store builds are foreclosed by hard rule 7, and a service worker is foreclosed by `no-bait.test.ts`. The founder gets a full-screen home-screen app with no browser bar; they do not get an App Store listing, and the reason is in their own brief.

DENSE FEEDS vs. THE ~1s SSR BUDGET — the SPA gets the full system; the public pages get a measured dialect (2 font faces, 1 shadow value, 4 icon glyphs, no avatar stacks, no JS). One design language, two budgets, and the difference is written down rather than discovered by a failed gate.
buildOrder: 1. TOKENS + FONTS ONLY (half a day, zero DOM change, and the founder sees a different app immediately). Rewrite `src/design/tokens.css`: new ground/ink/accent values, elevation vars, the five-value radius scale, the new type scale, the two new @font-face blocks. Commit the four woff2 files + their OFL licences to `public/fonts/` and the two .woff duplicates to `server/assets/fonts/` for satori. Update `tailwind.config.ts` (it reads the vars), `tokens.md`'s contrast table, and — in the SAME commit — all six hand-written copies of the ground hex: `index.html`, `manifest.json` ×2, and the three `<meta name="theme-color">` tags. `tokens.test.ts` will tell you if you missed one. RISK: zero e2e assertions touch colour or font; only screenshots change.

2. THE `cs-*` LAYER (1–2 days). Rewrite `src/index.css`'s component layer: add `.cs-card`, `.cs-meta`, `.cs-avatar(-stack)`, `.cs-rank-chip`, `.cs-tabbar`, `.cs-fab`, `.cs-sheet`, `.cs-segment`, `.cs-stat`, `.cs-tile`, `.cs-rail`, `.cs-skel`; restyle `.cs-chip` / `.cs-pill` / `.cs-pill-ghost` / `.cs-word` / `.cs-empty` IN PLACE so nothing importing them breaks. Keep `.cs-row` as a class name — it becomes a card — so the `li:not(:first-child) > .cs-row` hairline-restore rules and their guard test stay meaningful. Re-run `motion.test.ts` (every duration must be `var(--duration-*)`, every animation `fill: both`, every keyframe ending at rest, and the blanket reduced-motion block present) and `disabled.test.ts` (its PRESSABLE list is cs-pill / cs-pill-ghost / cs-word / cs-chip — all four survive; add `.cs-card` and `.cs-fab` to that one rule and to the test's list together).

3. THE ICON MODULE (half a day). `src/components/icons/{paths.ts,Icon.tsx,LICENSE}`. Then immediately run `no-scales.test.ts` — its glyph rule bans ★ ☆ ⭐ 👍 👎 and its import rule bans `@/components/ui/*` (which no longer exists) and `@radix-ui/react-slider|progress|radio-group`. Nothing here should trip it, and proving that now is cheaper than proving it after 14 screens use it.

4. THE SHELL (half a day, and this is the moment navigation stops being 'subpar'). `AppShell.tsx` → five slots + FAB. KEEP `data-shell`, and KEEP `data-tab="home|search|log|you"` and `data-log-entry` and `data-waiting` on their new elements — 13 `[data-tab]` and 8 `[data-log-entry]` assertions ride on those and the prefetch-on-pointerdown warming must survive or the log flow's six-tap budget breaks. ADD `data-tab="crew"`. The only tests to touch are the ones asserting the bar has exactly four children.

5. PLACE CARD (1 day). `src/components/discover/PlaceRow.tsx` → `PlaceCard`, plus `PlacePlate` restyled. KEEP every attribute: `data-place`, `data-place-row`, `data-shop-id`, `data-shop-slug`, `data-lead`, `data-stale`, `data-nophoto`, `data-who`. Add `data-cosign` on the cosign row and `data-rank` on the rank chip. 8 `[data-place-row]` + 4 `[data-place]` assertions pass untouched if you keep the attributes on the outer link. Screenshots regenerate.

6. HOME (1 day — the screen the founder opens). Hero card, the open-now rail, the crew feed section, the card feed. KEEP `data-home`, `data-state`, `data-phase`, `data-hero-mode`, `data-hero-query`, `data-hero-summary`, `data-ask-again`, `data-answer`, `data-last-call`, `data-elsewhere`, `data-order`, `data-moved`, `data-crowd-toggle`. Convert `data-crowd-toggle` from an underlined sentence to a chip pair — same attribute, same aria-pressed, so the 3 assertions hold. Do the PROSE CUT here in its own commit: three paragraphs → one 13px line each. Run `home.spec.ts` (44 tests) after, against a scratch DB.

7. THE PROSE PASS everywhere else (half a day, own commit). Search, Profile, ListDetail, GroupSession, PlaceFlow. Every explanatory paragraph becomes a chip, a meta value, or is deleted. Watch `.cs-ledger` — its value column is `white-space: nowrap` and a sentence in it makes the page scroll sideways, which `social.spec.ts` asserts against.

This is the largest single answer to 'not enough features' and it is mostly wiring. ruleCompliance: RULE 1 — NO RATING-SCALE INPUT. The icon set contains no star, heart, thumb, flame, gauge or bar-chart glyph, and level-shaped icons (wifi, sound) are drawn at full state only with the value carried by a labelled enum word beside them. Skeletons are static, so no progress-shaped animation exists. The `.cs-segment` control uses plain buttons with `aria-pressed`, never `role=radiogroup`. Step progress in the log flow stays a sentence — no dot row, no bar. The only number beside a place is `.cs-rank-chip`, which is a position in an ordered list. ENFORCED BY: `src/design/no-scales.test.ts` (range/number inputs, slider/progressbar/radiogroup roles, aria-value*, <progress>/<meter>, scale-primitive imports, the five banned glyphs, N/5 and N/10 scores).

RULE 2 — COSIGN = RANKING, NO STANDALONE ENDORSE. `.cs-cosign-row` is the densest social component in the direction and it contains zero buttons: an avatar stack plus a sentence naming who ranked the place. There is no like, heart, upvote, reply or repost anywhere in the component list, and no counter of anything a viewer can do to a post. The only place-level actions in the product are 'Rank it' and 'Log a visit'.

RULE 3 — NO ENGAGEMENT BAIT. No service worker, no push, no browser notifications, no polling refetch, no timers. The only count in the chrome is the ask count on the bell, which is raised solely by a friend request or a friend asking, never by elapsed time or by news, and is cleared by answering (where 'not now' answers it). Profile stats are three self-owned set sizes with no comparison and no leaderboard. ENFORCED BY: `src/design/no-bait.test.ts` (setInterval/refetchInterval/cron/serviceWorker/PushManager/Notification, streaks, badges, unread counts, points, levels, nudges, and absence-nag copy) — note it bans the literal word 'badge', so the ask count is named `asks` in code.

RULE 4 — RANK CANNOT BE BOUGHT. No sponsored slot, no promoted card, no ad shape in the component list. Home keeps its bottom line, restyled as an 11px gold small-caps label rather than deleted: 'Nothing here is scored, and nothing here was paid for.' The ordering on every surface is friend-weighted crowd rank computed server-side, and Home keeps the crowd-order toggle so the claim is auditable by the user.

RULE 5 — FRIENDS-ONLY BY DEFAULT. No visibility default changes. The new `share` action in the Profile and list app bars opens a sheet that creates, shows and REVOKES a per-list/profile token — surfacing the existing model, not widening it. Nothing on a public page is rendered that the token does not scope; the derived-order fix and the opaque group seat ids stay exactly as built.

RULE 6 — THE PUBLIC SSR PAGES STAY LIGHT. A measured cheap dialect: 2 font faces (preloaded, latin-basic, swap), 1 shadow value, ≤4 inline icon glyphs, no avatar stacks, no backdrop-filter, no carousel, no arrival cascade, no JS beyond the existing inline chip filter, and the tokens still inlined by `server/pages/tokens.ts` so there is zero stylesheet request. Sign-off requires the median of 5 Lighthouse runs, an LH_BLOCK font control, and a same-minute old-build control, with stray Chrome killed first. ENFORCED BY: `e2e/share.spec.ts` (zero /assets/*.js, zero stylesheets) and `scripts/lighthouse.mjs`'s non-zero exit.

RULE 7 — ZERO EXTERNAL SERVICES. Fonts are committed woff2/woff files with their OFL licences, as today. Icons are ~4kB of vendored SVG path data with the ISC licence copied in — lucide-react is NOT reinstalled. No CDN, no icon font, no analytics SDK, no map SDK, no Capacitor/Expo, no App Store build, no service worker. Dependency count does not rise.

RULE 8 — ACCESSIBILITY. 44px minimum on every target (chips reach it via an 8px ::before hit extension, avatar-only targets get an invisible 44px box, tab slots are 56×62, the FAB is 60). Contrast re-derived against --surface, not --bg: ink ~15:1, line 10.66:1, muted 6.34:1, gold 8.92:1, ember 5.25:1, and --bg on ember 5.78:1 for the FAB glyph. Focus is a 2px ember ring at 3px offset plus a 1px dark inner ring so it survives on ember grounds. Reduced motion is the existing blanket block zeroing the four duration tokens — sheets become instant, cards stop scaling, cascades stop. No colour-only meaning: every icon has adjacent text or an aria-label, the active tab has an ember glyph AND a drawn rule AND aria-current, a stale card has the word 'checked 3 weeks ago' and not just a hue. Remember axe reports contrast it cannot measure as 'incomplete', which never fails a gate — check hairline and label colours against tokens.md by hand, and always `settled(page)` AFTER `loaded(page, '[data-x]')`, twice with a frame between.
